questions.question: Define linear, superficial, and cubical expansivity. Derive the relationship between them.

questions.answer: **Linear expansivity (α):** the fractional increase in **length** per degree temperature rise: α = ΔL/(L ΔT), so ΔL = αLΔT; unit K⁻¹. **Superficial expansivity (β):** the fractional increase in **area** per degree rise: β = ΔA/(A ΔT); unit K⁻¹. **Cubical expansivity (γ):** the fractional increase in **volume** per degree rise: γ = ΔV/(V ΔT); unit K⁻¹. **Relationship:** consider a square of side L expanding to L(1 + αΔT): A′ = L²(1 + αΔT)² ≈ L²(1 + 2αΔT) (neglecting α²ΔT²) ⟹ ΔA/A = 2αΔT ⟹ **β = 2α**. Similarly a cube: V′ = L³(1 + αΔT)³ ≈ L³(1 + 3αΔT) ⟹ **γ = 3α**. Hence **α : β : γ = 1 : 2 : 3**. **Deep point:** the 1:2:3 ladder is just the binomial expansion of (1 + αΔT)ⁿ — area squares the length scale, volume cubes it; the cross terms are dropped because αΔT ~ 10⁻⁵ is tiny.

questions.question: Define the coefficient of linear expansivity and write its formula and SI unit.
questions.solution:
**Definition:** The coefficient of linear expansivity $\alpha$ of a solid is defined as the **increase in length per unit original length per unit rise in temperature**.

**Formula:**
$$\alpha = \frac{\Delta L}{L_0 \Delta T} = \frac{L_T - L_0}{L_0 \Delta T}$$
where $\Delta L = L_T - L_0$ is the change in length.

**From the new length:** $L_T = L_0(1 + \alpha\Delta T)$

**SI unit:** $\text{K}^{-1}$ or $^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$ (same, since a temperature interval of 1 K equals 1 degree Celsius). Dimensional formula: $\left[T^{-1}\right]$.

**Values:** Aluminium $\approx 23 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{K}^{-1}$, brass $\approx 19 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{K}^{-1}$, steel $\approx 11 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{K}^{-1}$, glass $\approx 9 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{K}^{-1}$.
questions.knowledgeNote: Linear expansivity is the fractional increase in length per degree rise in temperature, with SI unit per kelvin.
questions.answer: **Coefficient of linear expansivity (α):** the fractional increase in length per unit original length per degree rise in temperature — the increase in length of unit length when heated through 1 K. **Formula:** **α = ΔL/(L₀ ΔT)**, equivalently L = L₀(1 + αΔT). **SI unit: per kelvin (K⁻¹)** (equivalently °C⁻¹, since it is a per-degree quantity). Typical values: steel 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, invar ~10⁻⁶ K⁻¹. **Deep point:** α is small and the ΔT² corrections are negligible — that's why the linear formula works even for 100-degree rises, and why α : β : γ stays exactly 1 : 2 : 3.
